en: to be burdensome; to be cumbersome; to be troublesome

examples.en: The long skirt was cumbersome, so I changed into pants.
If you have a lot of luggage, travel becomes a hassle.
Please leave out the bulky packaging.
The gloves are so thick that they feel cumbersome.
If your clothes are cumbersome, it's hard to exercise.
I got a gift, but honestly it was a bit of a burden.

explain: 물건이나 일이 크거나 많아서 움직이기 불편하고 방해될 때 써요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '거추장스러워요', '거추장스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 사람에게 쓰면 '짐이 되는 존재'처럼 들려서 아주 거칠어요.

phrases.en: I don't want to wear clothes that get in the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거추장스럽다'를 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태예요. 옷, 짐, 장식 앞에 잘 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun; works well with clothes, luggage, or decorations.

phrases.en: The umbrella is so big that it's a nuisance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 해요체로 말하는 가장 기본 형태예요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙에 주의하세요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic polite spoken form; remember the ㅂ irregular change.

phrases.en: This bag is small, so it isn't a hassle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불편하지 않고 방해가 안 된다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that something isn't bothersome or in the way.

explain_en: Use it when something is bulky or excessive and gets in the way of moving or doing things. It is a ㅂ-irregular word, giving '거추장스러워요' and '거추장스러운'. Said about a person it sounds like calling them a burden, which is very harsh.

en: to be antique; to be old-fashioned

examples.ko: 이 카페는 분위기가 고풍스러워서 사진 찍기 좋아요.
examples.en: This cafe has an old-fashioned charm, so it's great for photos.

examples.ko: 고풍스러운 한옥에서 하룻밤 묵어 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd like to stay one night in an elegant old hanok.
The furniture is antique-looking and very elegant.
The hotel lobby is more classic-looking than I expected.

examples.ko: 고풍스럽게 꾸민 찻집이 골목 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: There's a tea house decorated in an old-style way at the end of the alley.
The outside looks antique, but the inside is very modern.

explain: 건물, 가구, 분위기에서 옛날 멋이 느껴질 때 칭찬으로 써요. 같은 오래된 물건이라도 '낡다'는 헐고 닳았다는 느낌이 강해서 칭찬이 아니에요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라 '고풍스러워요', '고풍스러운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.example: 시내에 고풍스러운 건물이 많아서 걷기 좋아요.
phrases.en: There are many antique-looking buildings downtown, so it's nice to walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 활용형이고 건물, 가구, 거리에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before nouns, fitting for buildings, furniture and streets.

phrases.en: This tea house's interior is really antique in style.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 분위기를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for praising an atmosphere.
phrases.en_equiv: it's old-fashioned in a nice way

phrases.en: It's a newly built building, so it doesn't feel antique.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 멋이 느껴지지 않을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when there is no old-style charm.

explain_en: Use it as praise when a building, furniture or atmosphere has old-time charm. Even for old things, '낡다' sounds worn and shabby, so it is not a compliment. It is a 'ㅂ' irregular adjective, so it becomes '고풍스러워요' and '고풍스러운'.

examples.ko: 도로 공사 현장에서 굴착기가 땅을 파고 있어요.
examples.en: An excavator is digging the ground at the road construction site.

examples.ko: 굴착기 소리가 시끄러워서 어젯밤에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The excavator noise was so loud that I couldn't sleep last night.

examples.ko: 하루 만에 굴착기로 큰 구덩이를 팠어요.
examples.en: They dug a huge hole with an excavator in a single day.

examples.ko: 굴착기의 긴 팔이 땅속 깊이 내려갔어요.
examples.en: The excavator's long arm went deep into the ground.
You need a license to operate an excavator.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 굴착기 장난감을 제일 좋아해요.
examples.en: My child likes excavator toys the best.

explain: 한국 사람들은 일상에서 '포클레인'이라고도 많이 불러요. '굴삭기'도 같은 기계를 가리키는데, 공식적인 글에서는 보통 '굴착기'를 써요.

phrases.en: An excavator is digging the ground at the construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 많이 쓰는 같은 기계의 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common everyday name for the same machine.

phrases.en: My uncle works as an excavator operator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계를 운전하는 사람을 말할 때 '기사'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 기사 to name the person who operates it.

phrases.en: They dug the ground deep with an excavator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 나타내는 '-로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the instrument particle -로.

explain_en: In daily life, Koreans also commonly call it a '포클레인' (after a brand name). '굴삭기' refers to the same machine, but formal writing usually uses '굴착기'.

examples.en: I found an old crate in the storeroom.

examples.ko: 할머니는 궤짝 안에 옛날 사진을 보관하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother kept old photos inside a wooden chest.
If you buy apples by the whole crate, it's much cheaper.
Among the moving boxes, the crate was the heaviest.
I took out the books in the crate and sorted them.
There's a chair made from a crate at the cafe.

explain: '상자'보다 옛날 가구나 시장, 창고에서 쓰는 큰 나무 상자 느낌이 강해요. '사과 궤짝', '생선 궤짝'처럼 물건을 담는 큰 통을 말할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 시장에 나무 궤짝이 높이 쌓여 있어요.
phrases.en: Wooden crates are stacked high at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 궤짝의 가장 흔한 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical image of a crate.

phrases.en: We loaded the apple crates onto the truck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일 이름을 앞에 붙여서 무엇을 담는 궤짝인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fruit name in front tells what the crate holds.

phrases.en: They put tangerines in crates and sell them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 큰 상자에 넣는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes putting goods into a large crate.

explain_en: Compared with '상자' (box), it feels more like an old piece of furniture or a large wooden box used in markets and warehouses. It is used for big containers, as in '사과 궤짝' (apple crate) or '생선 궤짝' (fish crate).

examples.ko: 저는 소리가 좋아서 기계식 키보드를 써요.
examples.en: I use a mechanical keyboard because I like the sound.

examples.ko: 이 시계는 배터리 없이 움직이는 기계식이에요.
examples.en: This watch is a mechanical one that runs without a battery.

examples.ko: 기계식 주차장은 좁은 땅에서도 많은 차를 세울 수 있어요.
examples.en: A mechanical parking lot can hold many cars even on a small plot of land.

examples.ko: 기계식으로 만든 장난감이라 건전지가 필요 없어요.
examples.en: It's a mechanically operated toy, so it needs no batteries.

examples.ko: 커피 머신은 전자식보다 기계식이 더 튼튼하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the mechanical type of coffee machine is sturdier than the electronic type.
My father still likes mechanical cameras.

explain: 전자식이나 디지털과 대비해서 부품이 직접 움직이는 방식을 말할 때 써요. 키보드, 시계, 주차장, 카메라 같은 말과 자주 나오고 반대 느낌의 말은 '전자식'이에요.

phrases.en: My grandfather gave me a mechanical watch as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배터리 없이 부품으로 움직이는 시계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a watch that runs on parts without a battery.

phrases.example: 기계식 주차장은 차를 자동으로 올려 줘요.
phrases.en: A mechanical parking garage lifts the car automatically.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 차를 옮겨 주는 주차장을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for a parking garage where machines move the car.

phrases.en: This camera isn't mechanical but electronic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형과 '전자식'을 함께 써서 방식의 차이를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form with '전자식' lets you contrast the two types.

explain_en: It is used in contrast to electronic or digital, for systems where parts physically move. It often goes with keyboards, watches, parking lots, and cameras, and the contrasting word is '전자식'.

examples.ko: 이 휴대폰에는 번역 기능이 내장되어 있어요.
examples.en: This phone has a translation function built in.
The laptop has a built-in camera, so it's convenient.

examples.ko: 스피커가 내장되어서 따로 살 필요가 없어요.
examples.en: Speakers are built in, so you don't need to buy them separately.

examples.ko: 앞으로 이 시계에는 심박수 장치가 내장될 거예요.
examples.en: From now on, this watch will have a heart rate sensor built in.
I bought a desk with a built-in outlet.
The manual says the battery is built in.

explain: 기계나 제품에 기능이 처음부터 안에 들어 있을 때 써요. '내장 카메라', '내장 메모리'처럼 앞에서 꾸미는 모양도 많아요. 밖에 따로 붙이는 것은 '외장'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: This watch has GPS in it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내장되어 있다'보다 쉽고 일상적으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, everyday way to say it's built in.

phrases.en: The built-in speaker is louder than I expected.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품 안에 처음부터 들어 있는 것을 꾸미는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier for something that comes inside the product.

phrases.en: This phone has plenty of built-in memory.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내장'이 앞에 붙어서 기계 안의 부품을 가리키는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase where 내장 before a noun marks a part inside the device.

explain_en: Use it when a feature is part of a device from the start. It often modifies nouns, as in 내장 카메라 or 내장 메모리. Something attached separately on the outside is called 외장.

en: to be translucent; to be semitransparent

examples.ko: 이 유리는 반투명해서 안이 흐릿하게 보여요.
examples.en: This glass is translucent, so you can see inside only dimly.

examples.ko: 욕실 문은 반투명한 유리로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The bathroom door is made of translucent glass.
To make it translucent, stick on a thin sheet of paper.
This plastic bag is semitransparent.
If the curtains are translucent, light comes in even during the day.

examples.ko: 그 병은 반투명하지만 안이 완전히 보이지는 않아요.
examples.en: That bottle is translucent, but you can't see inside completely.

explain: '투명하다'와 '불투명하다'의 중간으로, 빛은 통과하지만 뒤의 모습이 또렷하게 보이지 않을 때 써요. 뒤에 명사가 오면 '반투명한'으로 써요. 서리가 낀 유리나 얇은 종이, 비닐에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I covered the window with translucent plastic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '반투명한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, use '반투명한'.

phrases.example: 이 종이는 반투명하지 않아서 뒤가 안 보여요.
phrases.en: This paper isn't translucent, so you can't see through it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛이 거의 통과하지 않을 때 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used when almost no light passes through.

phrases.en: The glass looks translucent because of the frost.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 그렇게 보일 때 '-해 보이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-해 보이다' when it simply looks that way.

explain_en: It sits between '투명하다' (transparent) and '불투명하다' (opaque): light passes through but what is behind is not clearly visible. Before a noun it becomes '반투명한'. It suits frosted glass, thin paper and plastic.

examples.en: The scale turned on with a beeping sound.
The fridge door is open, so it's beeping.
The alarm kept beeping from morning, so it was noisy.
The machine keeps beeping. What's wrong?
The toy whistle keeps squeaking, and the child loves it.

examples.ko: 화재 경보기가 삑삑거려서 모두 밖으로 나갔어요.
examples.en: The fire alarm started beeping, so everyone went outside.

explain: 알람이나 경고음, 호루라기 같은 기계 소리에 주로 써요. 한 번 나면 '삑 소리가 나다'라고 하고, 사람이 높고 날카롭게 소리를 지르면 '빽빽거리다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I can hear a beeping sound outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삑삑거리다'를 꾸미는 말로 바꿔 소리를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used to describe a sound.

phrases.en: When the battery got weak, the smoke alarm started to beep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용하던 기계에서 소리가 나기 시작하는 순간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the moment a quiet machine starts making noise.

phrases.example: 기계가 밤새 삑삑거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
phrases.en: The machine beeped all night, so I couldn't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 계속 나서 불편할 때 이유를 붙여 말하기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Handy for giving a reason when a continuous sound is bothersome.
phrases.en_equiv: to beep so much one can't sleep

explain_en: It is mainly used for machine sounds such as alarms, warning beeps and whistles. A single sound is '삑 소리가 나다', and when a person yells in a high, sharp voice, '빽빽거리다' is used.

examples.en: If you rub the wood surface with sandpaper, it gets smooth.
The sandpaper is rough, so my hand hurts.
I bought sandpaper to strip off the paint.
I sanded for a long time, so my arm hurts.

examples.ko: 사포 번호가 높을수록 더 곱게 갈려요.
examples.en: The higher the sandpaper number, the finer it sands.

examples.ko: 이 사포는 철에도 쓸 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can this sandpaper be used on metal too?

explain: 가구, 벽, 나무를 매끈하게 다듬을 때 써요. '사포질하다', '사포로 갈다/문지르다'처럼 말하고, 가게에서는 번호로 거칠기를 말해요.

phrases.en: I sanded the chair and then painted it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사포로 표면을 다듬는 일을 한 단어로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: One word for smoothing a surface with sandpaper.

phrases.en: I sanded the rough part with sandpaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: '문지르다'와 비슷하게, 표면을 깎아 매끈하게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 문지르다, used for wearing a surface smooth.

phrases.en: Please lend me one sheet of sandpaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사포는 얇은 종이 모양이라 '장'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sandpaper is counted in sheets with 장.

explain_en: It is used to smooth furniture, walls and wood. People say '사포질하다' or '사포로 갈다/문지르다', and in shops the roughness is given by a number.

examples.en: Semiconductors are made of silicon.

examples.ko: 주방에서 실리콘 장갑을 써서 손을 안 데었어요.
examples.en: I used silicone gloves in the kitchen, so I didn't burn my hand.
The phone case is silicone, so it is soft and bendy.

examples.ko: 실리콘 접시는 접어서 가방에 넣을 수 있어요.
examples.en: A silicone plate can be folded and put in a bag.

examples.ko: 욕실 틈에 실리콘을 발랐더니 물이 안 새요.
examples.en: After I put silicone sealant in the bathroom gaps, water no longer leaks.

examples.ko: 실리콘 밸리는 미국에 있는 유명한 지역이에요.
examples.en: Silicon Valley is a famous area in the United States.

explain: 한국어 '실리콘' 하나가 영어의 silicon(반도체 재료)과 silicone(부드러운 고무 같은 재료)을 둘 다 가리켜요. 반도체 이야기면 앞의 것이고, 주방용품이나 휴대폰 케이스, 접착제 이야기면 뒤의 것이에요.

phrases.example: 컴퓨터 안에는 작은 실리콘 칩이 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a small silicon chip inside the computer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전자 부품 이야기에서 반도체 재료로서의 실리콘이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Silicon as a semiconductor material in talk of electronic parts.

phrases.en: I put a silicone case on my new phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부드러운 고무 같은 재료로 만든 물건 이야기예요.
phrases.nuance_en: About objects made of the soft, rubber-like material.

phrases.en: A silicone spatula is safe even on a hot pan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주방용품에서는 부드러운 재료 실리콘을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In kitchenware, it means the soft material silicone.

explain_en: The one Korean word 실리콘 covers both English silicon (the chip material) and silicone (the soft, rubbery material). Context tells you which: chips mean silicon, while kitchenware, phone cases, and sealant mean silicone.

examples.ko: 대문을 여닫는 소리가 들리는 걸 보니 아들이 외출하나 봐요.
examples.en: I hear the gate opening and closing, so my son must be going out.

examples.ko: 서랍을 자꾸 여닫지 말고 필요한 것만 꺼내세요.
examples.en: Don't keep opening and closing the drawer; just take out what you need.

examples.ko: 문을 세게 여닫으면 이웃에게 방해가 돼요.
examples.en: If you open and close the door hard, it disturbs the neighbors.

examples.ko: 문을 하루에도 몇 번씩 여닫아도 고장 안 나요.
examples.en: Even if you open and close the door several times a day, it won't break.

examples.ko: 창문을 여닫을 때 손이 끼지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to get your hand caught when you open and close the window.
I want to buy a bag that's easy to open and close.

explain: 문, 서랍, 창문, 뚜껑처럼 열고 닫는 것에 써요. 한 번 열기만 할 때는 '열다', 닫기만 할 때는 '닫다'를 써요. 열고 닫는 동작이 반복되거나 함께 이어질 때 '여닫다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The sound of the door opening and closing is too loud.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 소리'를 붙여 반복되는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -는 소리 describes a repeated sound.

phrases.en: Please don't open and close the refrigerator door so often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 열고 닫는 행동을 하지 말라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to open and close something repeatedly.

phrases.en: I opened and closed the window several times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 열고 닫는 동작을 했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for an opening-and-closing action.

explain_en: Use it for things that open and shut, such as doors, drawers, windows and lids. When you only open, use '열다', and when you only close, use '닫다'. '여닫다' is natural when the opening and closing happens repeatedly or together.

examples.ko: 용광로에서 쇠가 녹아서 빨간 물처럼 흘러요.
examples.en: Iron melts in the blast furnace and flows like red water.

examples.ko: 제철소에 가면 커다란 용광로를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to a steel mill, you can see a huge blast furnace.

examples.ko: 용광로 안은 온도가 천 도가 넘어요.
examples.en: The temperature inside the blast furnace is over a thousand degrees.
The classroom is as hot as a furnace today.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 여러 문화가 섞인 용광로예요.
examples.en: This city is a melting pot where many cultures mix.

examples.ko: 용광로 앞에서 일하는 사람들은 특별한 옷을 입어요.
examples.en: People who work in front of the furnace wear special clothes.

explain: '용광로처럼 덥다'처럼 아주 뜨거운 곳을 비유할 때 써요. '문화의 용광로'처럼 여러 사람과 문화가 한곳에 섞여 있는 곳을 말할 때도 많이 써요. 영어의 'melting pot'과 비슷해요.

phrases.example: 여름 한낮의 버스 안은 용광로처럼 뜨거워요.
phrases.en: The inside of a bus at midday in summer is as hot as a furnace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 뜨거운 곳을 과장해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to exaggerate how hot a place is.

phrases.en: New York is called a melting pot of cultures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 문화와 사람이 한곳에 섞여 있다는 뜻의 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor meaning many cultures and people are mixed in one place.

phrases.en: At the factory they melt iron in a blast furnace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 제철소에서 쇠를 녹이는 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the actual process of melting iron at a steel mill.

explain_en: It is used as a metaphor for a very hot place, as in '용광로처럼 덥다'. It also appears in '문화의 용광로' for a place where many people and cultures mix, similar to the English 'melting pot'.

en: to be equipped; to be fitted; to be embedded

examples.en: A camera is fitted on new cars.
This phone is equipped with a big battery.

examples.ko: 내년에는 안전 장치가 모두 장착될 거예요.
examples.en: Next year all the safety devices will be installed.
The fitted parts are different, so the prices differ too.

examples.ko: 렌즈가 장착되고 나서 사진이 더 선명해졌어요.
examples.en: After the lens was attached, the photos got sharper.
Airbags are installed, so it is safer.

explain: 제품 소개나 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '달려 있다', '들어 있다'를 더 많이 써요. 사람이 달면 '장착하다', 달려 있는 상태가 되면 '장착되다'예요. '카메라가 장착된 차'처럼 뒤 명사를 꾸며 주는 모양으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I bought a car equipped with airbags.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤 명사를 꾸며 줘요. 제품 소개에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies the noun that follows. Common in product descriptions.

phrases.en: A sensor is fitted as standard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 달려 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where something is already attached.

phrases.en: This car has a camera on it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장착되다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word that is more common than 'jangchakdoeda' in daily talk.

explain_en: It appears often in product descriptions and the news; in everyday talk Koreans say '달려 있다' or '들어 있다' more often. The person who installs it uses '장착하다'; the part that ends up installed is '장착되다'. It is also common as a modifier, as in '카메라가 장착된 차' (a car fitted with a camera).

examples.ko: 공사장에서 중장비 소리가 하루 종일 들려요.
examples.en: The sound of heavy machinery can be heard all day at the construction site.
You need a license to become a heavy equipment operator.

examples.ko: 큰 눈이 와서 중장비로 길을 치웠어요.
examples.en: A lot of snow fell, so they cleared the road with heavy machinery.
Heavy machinery has difficulty getting into narrow alleys.
Heavy machinery was brought in to the landslide site.

examples.ko: 중장비를 빌리는 데 하루에 얼마나 들어요?
examples.en: How much does it cost per day to rent heavy equipment?

explain: 굴착기, 크레인, 불도저처럼 공사나 구조 현장에서 쓰는 크고 무거운 기계를 한꺼번에 부르는 말이에요. 뉴스나 공사 이야기에서 '중장비 투입', '중장비 기사'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Heavy machinery was sent to the accident site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사나 구조 현장에 기계를 보낼 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news when machines are sent to a work or rescue site.

phrases.en: I'm learning to operate heavy machinery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계를 움직이는 일이나 기술을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the work or skill of operating the machines.

phrases.en: They are digging the ground with heavy machinery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계로 하는 공사 일을 구체적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe construction work done with machines.

explain_en: It is a group name for big, heavy machines used at construction or rescue sites, like excavators, cranes and bulldozers. It often appears in news and construction talk, as in '중장비 투입' (heavy machinery deployed) and '중장비 기사' (equipment operator).

examples.ko: 이 측정기로 방의 온도를 재 봐요.
examples.en: I measure the room temperature with this instrument.
At the hospital they checked me with a blood pressure monitor.

examples.ko: 새로 산 측정기가 고장 나서 바꿔 왔어요.
examples.en: The new meter I bought broke, so I exchanged it.
The red light came on on the fine dust meter.

examples.ko: 측정기 사용법을 모르면 설명서를 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: If you don't know how to use the meter, read the manual.

examples.ko: 아버지가 사 오신 측정기는 작고 가벼워요.
examples.en: The meter my father bought is small and light.

explain: 온도계, 체중계, 혈압계처럼 재는 도구 이름에는 '-계'가 많이 붙고, '-기'는 기계 느낌이 강한 도구에 붙어요. 보통 '미세먼지 측정기'처럼 재는 대상을 앞에 붙여서 말해요.

phrases.en: I checked the air with a fine dust measuring device.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재는 대상을 앞에 붙여 어떤 도구인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put what is measured in front to say which instrument it is.

phrases.en: I measured the room humidity with a measuring instrument.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 써서 잰다는 뜻으로 '-(으)로'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -(으)로 to mean measuring by using the tool.

phrases.en: We use a measuring instrument when testing the air.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 사용하는 일을 간단히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple way to talk about using the tool.

explain_en: Measuring tools often end in '-계' (온도계, 체중계, 혈압계), while '-기' suggests more of a machine. Koreans usually put what is being measured in front, as in '미세먼지 측정기' (fine dust meter).

examples.en: The bridge could not bear the load.
This shelf's load limit is 20 kilograms.

examples.ko: 하중이 한쪽에 몰리면 무너질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the load is concentrated on one side, it can collapse.
The floor sank a little because of the load.
The truck unloaded cargo to reduce the load.
When snow piles up, the load on the roof increases.

explain: 하중은 건물, 다리, 선반처럼 구조물이 버티는 무게예요. 사람 몸무게나 물건 무게는 보통 '무게'라고 하고, 하중은 구조가 견디는 힘을 이야기할 때 나와요. '최대 하중'은 안전 표시에서 자주 봐요.

phrases.example: 이 다리는 큰 하중을 견딜 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This bridge can bear a heavy load.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구조물이 무게를 버틴다는 뜻으로, 하중과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common collocation with 하중 and means a structure holds up under weight.

phrases.example: 엘리베이터 안에 최대 하중이 적혀 있어요.
phrases.en: The maximum load is written inside the elevator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 표시에서 자주 보는 말로, 구조물이 견딜 수 있는 가장 큰 무게예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen on safety signs, meaning the greatest weight a structure can safely hold.

phrases.en: Too much load was put on the pillar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무게가 구조물에 실려서 힘을 받는다는 뜻으로, 하중이 그 자리에 작용할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means weight is placed on a structure so that it bears the force.

explain_en: 하중 is the weight that a structure such as a building, bridge, or shelf has to bear. A person's body weight or an object's weight is normally 무게, and 하중 comes up when talking about how much a structure can hold. You often see 최대 하중 on safety labels.

examples.en: When I stepped into the room, a faint fragrance was in the air.
After visiting a temple, the scent of incense soaks into my clothes.

examples.ko: 어디서 이렇게 좋은 향내를 풍기는 걸까요?
examples.en: Where is such a nice scent coming from?

examples.ko: 꽃에서 나는 향내는 아침에 더 진해요.
examples.en: The scent of flowers is stronger in the morning.
Intoxicated by the fragrance, I closed my eyes for a moment.

examples.ko: 이 비누는 향내도 좋고 거품도 잘 나요.
examples.en: This soap smells nice and lathers well too.

explain: '향기'는 좋은 냄새를 넓게 말하고, '향내'는 향이나 꽃에서 나는 냄새를 말할 때 더 자주 써요. '향내가 나다', '향내를 풍기다', '향내가 배다'처럼 말해요. 좋은 냄새에만 쓰고 나쁜 냄새에는 '냄새'나 '악취'를 써요.

phrases.example: 꽃들이 봄이 되자 은은한 향내를 풍겨요.
phrases.en: When spring comes, the flowers give off a soft fragrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 향이나 꽃이 냄새를 퍼뜨릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when incense or flowers spread their scent.

phrases.example: 문을 열자마자 향내를 맡을 수 있었어요.
phrases.en: I could smell the fragrance as soon as I opened the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새를 받아들이는 사람의 입장에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the point of view of the person who smells it.

phrases.example: 이 방은 향내가 짙어서 머리가 아파요.
phrases.en: This room has such a strong scent that my head hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 향이 진하게 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the scent is strong.

explain_en: '향기' covers pleasant smells in general, while '향내' is used more for the smell of incense or flowers. Typical phrases are '향내가 나다', '향내를 풍기다' and '향내가 배다'. It is only for good smells; for bad ones use '냄새' or '악취'.
